newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran rejects fresh claim of Lockerbie involvement.
newsitem.headline: Iran rejects fresh claim of Lockerbie involvement.

text.p: Germany's federal crime office is investigating claims by a former Iranian spy that Tehran was behind the bombing of a Pan Am Boeing 747 which crashed to earth in Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988, a German magazine reported.
Iran rejected what it called the "old allegations", describing them as Zionist propaganda.

In an article to appear in Monday's edition of Der Spiegel, a 39-year-old former spy named Abolghasem Mesbahi was quoted as telling the German crime office (BKA) that Iran planned the attack as revenge after the U.S. cruiser Vincennes shot down an Iran Air Airbus over the Strait of Hormuz earlier in 1988.
The U.S. cruiser mistakenly shot down the Iran Air plane, killing the 290 people aboard, because it thought it was an Iranian military plane.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi said the allegations attributed to Mesbahi, known in Germany as Witness C, were part of an anti-Iran propaganda campaign by German media.

"The Witness C has turned into a tool in the hands of German media to serve the interests of the Zionists by fabricating unfounded and ridiculous allegations against Iran when the Zionist regime so wishes," the Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Mohammadi as saying.
Der Spiegel's report said Mesbahi told the BKA that parts for the bomb that blew up the Pan Am flight were put on a plane at Frankfurt airport.
The bomb parts were put together in London and loaded onto the ill-fated Pan Am flight, Mesbahi told BKA, according to Der Spiegel. A total of 270 people were killed in the Lockerbie bombing.

Mesbahi said that Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini personally ordered the revenge attack and that Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati had carried out the planning with Libya and guerrilla leader Abu Nidal, Der Spiegel said.

It said that the BKA, Germany's BND intelligence agency, and the office for the protection of the constitution (BfV) were investigating Mesbahi's statements. They said they were looking for evidence that either supports or refutes Mesbahi's claims.
No officials could be reached at the BKA or BND, and the German government press office declined to comment.

Mesbahi was a key witness for the German federal prosecutor in an April court case which concluded that Iran's top leaders had ordered the 1992 assassination of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran vehemently denied involvement in the killings.
Der Spiegel said Mesbahi had been provided with bodyguards from the BKA.
